newsitem.title: USA: Storm damage delays reopen of Colonial Line-4.
newsitem.headline: Storm damage delays reopen of Colonial Line-4.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline said the reopening of its Line Four section was delayed due to damage caused by the tropical storm which passed through Friday.

The portion of the Colonial pipeline, which carries refined products from Greensboro, North Carolina north to the Baltimore area, was shut by a power outage earlier. The line had been expected back up hours ago but would remain shut until around 1700 EDT/2100 GMT as water-damaged underground cables were repaired, according to a Colonial spokesperson.
"Power is working in the Greensboro area but cables blew and are having to be replaced," she said.

Colonial's product lines carry nearly two million barrels per day (bpd) of gasoline and distillates from Houston to Greenboro, N.C. and to Linden, N.J. near the New York Harbor delivery points for NYMEX heating oil and gasoline futures.
The pipeline's flows north of Baltimore were not interrupted by the damage to Line 4, Colonial said earlier.
